explanation: In a static fluid the pressure increases linearly with depth because each layer must support the weight of all the fluid above it: P = P0 + rho*g*h, where P0 is the pressure at the surface (atmospheric, ~101 kPa for an open container), rho is the fluid density, g is gravity, and h is the depth. The term rho*g*h is the gauge pressure — the amount ABOVE atmospheric — so absolute pressure is P0 plus the gauge term. Pressure depends only on depth h, not on the shape or total amount of the container (the hydrostatic paradox), and it acts equally in all directions. On the AP exam you add P0 for absolute pressure, drop it when only gauge pressure is asked, and use rho_water = 1000 kg/m^3 with the linear P-vs-h relationship shown by the straight line.
bullets: Pressure grows LINEARLY with depth h — the right-hand graph is a straight line.
rho*g*h is gauge pressure (above atmospheric); add P0 for absolute.
Depends only on h, not the container's shape or width.
The orange diver marker reads P at its current depth in kPa.
